paras.text: Topic: 時間（時點、時段） telling time — points in time and stretches of time
• Ask what time it is and say the time.
• Say when and where something happens, and from when to when.
• Make plans and set a time to meet with friends.
• Talk about things you do regularly.
Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue I. The book’s own Dialogue I is on book p. 132 (PDF p. 159); its recording is track 07-01.

lines.py: Yíjūn, nǐ hòutiān yǒu kòng ma?
Yǒu kòng. Shénme shì?

lines.zh: 我和朋友要去大安KTV唱歌，妳想不想一起去？
lines.py: Wǒ hàn péngyǒu yào qù Dà’ān KTV chànggē, nǐ xiǎng bù xiǎng yìqǐ qù?
Hǎo a! Nǐmen shénme shíhòu qù?
Cóng zhōngwǔ shí’èr diǎn dào wǔ diǎn.

lines.zh: 中午我得去銀行。我一點二十分到，好不好？
lines.py: Zhōngwǔ wǒ děi qù yínháng. Wǒ yì diǎn èrshí fēn dào, hǎo bù hǎo?

lines.zh: 沒問題。我們在KTV前面見面。
lines.py: Méi wèntí. Wǒmen zài KTV qiánmiàn jiànmiàn.
Duìle, Yuèměi yě qù ma?
Tā hòutiān yào shàngkè, xià cì ba.
Hǎo, hòutiān jiàn! Zàijiàn!

translation.en: Yijun, are you free the day after tomorrow?
Yes, I am. What’s up?
My friends and I are going to sing at Da-an KTV. Do you want to come along?
Sure! When are you going?
From twelve noon until five.
I have to go to the bank at noon. Is it OK if I get there at 1:20?
No problem. Let’s meet in front of the KTV.
By the way, is Yuemei coming too?
She has class that day — next time, maybe.
OK, see you the day after tomorrow! Bye!

items.en: Da’an — a district of Taipei; here, the name of a KTV
to be free, to have time

paras.text: Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue II. The book’s own Dialogue II is on book p. 135 (PDF p. 162); its recording is track 07-03.

lines.py: Āntóng, nǐ zài zuò shénme?

lines.zh: 我在寫字。我最近開始上書法課。
lines.py: Wǒ zài xiě zì. Wǒ zuìjìn kāishǐ shàng shūfǎ kè.
Yǒu yìsi! Nǐ měi tiān dōu xiě ma?

lines.zh: 對，每天中午都寫，從十二點到十二點半。
lines.py: Duì, měi tiān zhōngwǔ dōu xiě, cóng shí’èr diǎn dào shí’èr diǎn bàn.
Nǐ shénme shíhòu chī wǔcān?

lines.zh: 等一下。我剛下課，下午兩點有課。妳呢？最近忙不忙？
lines.py: Děng yíxià. Wǒ gāng xiàkè, xiàwǔ liǎng diǎn yǒu kè. Nǐ ne? Zuìjìn máng bù máng?

lines.zh: 很忙。今天下午我有事，得去打籃球比賽。
lines.py: Hěn máng. Jīntiān xiàwǔ wǒ yǒu shì, děi qù dǎ lánqiú bǐsài.

lines.zh: 比賽幾點開始？幾點結束？
lines.py: Bǐsài jǐ diǎn kāishǐ? Jǐ diǎn jiéshù?
Sì diǎn kāishǐ, wǔ diǎn bàn jiéshù.
Wǒ kěyǐ qù kàn ma?
Kěyǐ a! Huānyíng nǐ lái.

translation.en: Antong, what are you doing?
I’m writing characters. I’ve just started a calligraphy class.
How interesting! Do you write every day?
Yes, every day at noon, from twelve to half past twelve.
When do you have lunch?
In a little while. I’ve just come out of class, and I have another one at two. How about you — busy lately?
Very. I’m tied up this afternoon: I have to play in a basketball game.
What time does the game start? When does it end?
It starts at four and finishes at five thirty.
May I come and watch?
Of course! You’re welcome to come.

items.en: (marks an action in progress) to be …-ing
to finish class, class is over
to be busy, to have something on

paras.text: Clock times use 點 for the hour and 分 for minutes; 半 means half past. A time-of-day word goes in front: 早上 (morning), 中午 (noon), 下午 (afternoon), 晚上 (evening).
Note: for 2 o’clock say 兩點, not *二點. But 12 o’clock is 十二點, and in 2:22 only the hour takes 兩: 兩點二十二分.
To ask the time: 現在幾點？ “What time is it now?” — 幾點 “what hour”, 幾點幾分 “what hour and minute”.

blocks.en: I. Word order: time — place — event

paras.text: Use: When a sentence says both when and where something happens, the order is fixed: TIME before PLACE, and both before the action. The subject can stand at the very beginning or right after the time word.
Pattern: (Subject) + Time + (Subject) + Place + Action

items.en: I’m going to read at home tomorrow.

items.py: Tāmen wǎnshàng qī diǎn dào KTV chànggē.
items.en: They’re going to sing at KTV at seven this evening.

items.zh: 今天下午我們在圖書館見面。
items.py: Jīntiān xiàwǔ wǒmen zài túshūguǎn jiànmiàn.
items.en: We’re meeting at the library this afternoon.

items.zh: 我今天晚上不在家吃飯。
items.py: Wǒ jīntiān wǎnshàng bú zài jiā chīfàn.
items.en: I’m not eating at home tonight.

items.py: Tā zhōumò bú dào xuéxiào lái.
items.en: He doesn’t come to school on weekends.

items.py: Nǐmen jǐ diǎn zài nǎlǐ jiànmiàn?
items.en: What time and where are you meeting?

items.zh: 你明天要不要來我家吃飯？
items.py: Nǐ míngtiān yào bú yào lái wǒ jiā chīfàn?
items.en: Do you want to come and eat at my place tomorrow?

paras.text: Usage notes:
1. Time never comes after the place or the verb: 我晚上在家吃飯 is right; *我在家晚上吃飯 and *我在家吃飯晚上 are not.
2. If no time or place is mentioned, “now” and “here” are understood, or the context fills them in.
3. With 去 / 來, two orders are correct: 我們晚上去KTV唱歌 and 我們晚上到KTV去唱歌. In Taiwan the first is the more common one.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Put the parts in the correct order.

items.prompt: 在圖書館 ① ／ 下午 ② ／ 我 ③ ／ 寫書法 ④ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
見面 ① ／ 在KTV前面 ② ／ 晚上七點 ③ ／ 我們 ④ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
不 ① ／ 在家 ② ／ 他 ③ ／ 今天中午 ④ ／ 吃午餐 ⑤ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Answer with a time and a place.

blocks.en: II. 從 cóng … 到 dào …: from … to …

paras.text: Use: 從 A 到 B marks a range — either a stretch of time (from 9 to 12) or a distance between two places (from the dorm to the classroom).

items.zh: 我從早上九點到中午十二點有課。
items.py: Wǒ cóng zǎoshàng jiǔ diǎn dào zhōngwǔ shí’èr diǎn yǒu kè.
items.en: I have class from 9 a.m. to noon.

items.zh: 書法課從下午兩點到四點。
items.py: Shūfǎ kè cóng xiàwǔ liǎng diǎn dào sì diǎn.
items.en: Calligraphy class is from 2 to 4 p.m.

items.py: Cóng sùshè dào jiàoshì hěn jìn.
items.en: It’s close from the dorm to the classroom.

items.py: Tā cóng xuéxiào dào yínháng qù.
items.en: He’s going from school to the bank.

items.py: Cóng zhèlǐ dào KTV bù yuǎn.
items.en: It isn’t far from here to the KTV.

items.zh: 我們的書法課不是從一點到三點。
items.py: Wǒmen de shūfǎ kè búshì cóng yì diǎn dào sān diǎn.
items.en: Our calligraphy class isn’t from one to three.

items.zh: 我不想從學校去，我想從家裡去。
items.py: Wǒ bù xiǎng cóng xuéxiào qù, wǒ xiǎng cóng jiālǐ qù.
items.en: I don’t want to go from school; I want to go from home.

items.py: Nǐ cóng jǐ diǎn dào jǐ diǎn yǒu kòng?
items.en: From what time to what time are you free?

items.py: Cóng nǐ jiā dào xuéxiào yuǎn bù yuǎn?
items.en: Is it far from your home to school?

items.zh: 你從家裡來還是從學校來？
items.py: Nǐ cóng jiālǐ lái háishì cóng xuéxiào lái?
items.en: Are you coming from home or from school?

blocks.title: Questions (with 嗎, A-not-A, or 還是)
練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Make a sentence with 從…到….

items.prompt: A：你從幾點到幾點上網？　B：＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: III. 在 zài + action: an action in progress

paras.text: Use: 在 placed right before an action verb shows that the action is going on — now, or at the time mentioned in the sentence. It works like English “be …-ing”.

items.zh: 昨天晚上八點我在寫字。
items.py: Zuótiān wǎnshàng bā diǎn wǒ zài xiě zì.
items.en: At eight last night I was writing characters.

items.zh: 他不是在看電影，他在看比賽。
items.py: Tā búshì zài kàn diànyǐng, tā zài kàn bǐsài.
items.en: He isn’t watching a movie; he’s watching a game.

items.zh: 我不是在上網，我在寫書法。
items.py: Wǒ búshì zài shàngwǎng, wǒ zài xiě shūfǎ.
items.en: I’m not online; I’m doing calligraphy.
Is the teacher in class right now?

paras.text: Usage notes:
1. Only action verbs take this 在. State verbs do not: *咖啡在好喝, *手機在貴 are wrong.
2. Don’t mix this up with 在 + place (“at”). In 他在圖書館看書 “he reads in the library”, 在 introduces a place. In 他在看書 “he is reading”, 在 shows the action is going on.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Say what each person is doing right now.

items.prompt: A：你在看書嗎？（✗ 上網）　B：＿＿＿＿＿＿。

paras.text: Use: 每 means “every / each”. It is followed by a measure word and a noun, and the sentence almost always has 都 before the verb, stressing “without exception”.
Pattern: 每 + (一) + Measure word + Noun + 都 + Verb

items.py: Wǒ měi tiān dōu hē kāfēi.
Měi ge xuéshēng dōu yǒu shǒujī.

items.zh: 這家店，每杯咖啡都很好喝。
items.py: Zhè jiā diàn, měi bēi kāfēi dōu hěn hǎohē.
items.en: At this shop, every cup of coffee is good.

items.py: Tā měi ge zhōumò dōu qù yóuyǒng.
Tā měi tiān dōu bù máng.
items.en: He isn’t busy on any day.

items.py: Wǒ měi ge zhōumò dōu méi kòng.
items.en: I’m not free on any weekend.

items.zh: 我不是每天都上書法課。
items.py: Wǒ búshì měi tiān dōu shàng shūfǎ kè.
items.en: It’s not that I have calligraphy class every day.

blocks.title: Negation (不／沒 after 都; 不是 before 每 = “not every”)

items.zh: 你每天都在家吃晚飯嗎？
items.py: Nǐ měi tiān dōu zài jiā chī wǎnfàn ma?
items.en: Do you eat dinner at home every day?

items.py: Tā měi ge zhōumò dōu qù nǎlǐ?
items.en: Where does he go every weekend?

paras.text: Usage notes:
1. 天 is itself a measure word, so it follows 每 directly: 每天, not *每個天. The same holds for 每年 (every year).
2. 一 is often dropped: 每天 = 每一天, 每個 = 每一個.
3. Mind the position of the negative: 每天都不… means “never on any day”, while 不是每天都… means “not every day”.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete the sentences with 每…都….

items.prompt: 這家店的甜點，＿＿＿＿＿＿很好吃。（every one）
A：你每天都很忙嗎？　B：不，我不是＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: V. 可以 kěyǐ: may, be allowed to

paras.text: Use: The auxiliary verb 可以 gives or asks for permission. It goes before the main verb.

items.zh: 老師說，我們可以在教室吃午餐。
items.py: Lǎoshī shuō, wǒmen kěyǐ zài jiàoshì chī wǔcān.
items.en: The teacher says we may eat lunch in the classroom.

items.py: Nǐ kěyǐ kàn wǒ de shū.

items.zh: 你不可以在圖書館唱歌。
items.py: Nǐ bù kěyǐ zài túshūguǎn chànggē.
items.en: You’re not allowed to sing in the library.

items.zh: 對不起，這裡不可以照相。

a.zh: 我可不可以去看你的比賽？
a.py: Wǒ kě bù kěyǐ qù kàn nǐ de bǐsài?
a.en: May I come and watch your game?

a.zh: 我可以問你一個問題嗎？
a.py: Wǒ kěyǐ wèn nǐ yí ge wèntí ma?
a.en: May I ask you a question?

paras.text: Usage notes:
1. Earlier, 可以 also meant “it is possible to …” (看電影可以學中文 “you can learn Chinese by watching movies”). In this lesson it asks for or gives permission.
2. 不可以 only means “not allowed”. To say that something is not possible, Chinese normally uses 不能: 我的手機不能照相 “my phone can’t take pictures”.
3. A short answer to a 可以 question is just 可以 or 不可以.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete the dialogues with 可以 / 不可以 / 可不可以.

items.prompt: A：我＿＿＿＿在這裡喝咖啡？　B：＿＿＿＿，這裡是圖書館。
A：媽媽，我週末＿＿＿＿去朋友家？　B：＿＿＿＿，可是你得先去銀行。
A：老師，我們＿＿＿＿＿＿在教室吃午餐嗎？　B：＿＿＿＿。

paras.text: Goal: Describe an action in progress.
Task: One student mimes an action (singing, writing characters, playing basketball, cooking…). The others guess with 你在…嗎？ The mime answers 對，我在… or 我不是在…. The first correct guesser mimes next.
Goal: Say what you do at certain times and during certain periods.

Task: Fill in the timetable for one of your days, then describe it to a partner using time — place — event and 從…到…, e.g. 我從九點到十二點在學校上課。Your partner notes down your day and reports one thing to the class.
Goal: Talk about things done regularly; ask and tell the time.
Task: Ask classmates which of these they do every day, and when and where. Then tell the class one thing everybody does (每個人都…) and one thing nobody does every day.
Goal: Make an appointment with a friend.

Task: In pairs, plan a weekend outing. You must agree on what to do, the day, the time and the meeting place, and one of you must first suggest a time that doesn’t work. Write down your dialogue (about 8–10 lines) and act it out.
Useful words: 有空、沒空、有事、最近、可以、在哪裡、什麼時候、幾點、從…到…、下次吧、沒問題、再見
Goal: Describe when and where an activity takes place.

Task: Design a poster for a club (choir, basketball, calligraphy, cooking…). Include the practice days and times, the place, and what members need to be able to do (e.g. 會游泳). Present it; classmates ask questions such as 每天都練習嗎？從幾點到幾點？在哪裡？可以…嗎？

In Taiwan, “KTV” means a karaoke place where a group rents a private room by the hour, rather than singing on a stage in front of strangers. Going to KTV is a favourite pastime for students, families and colleagues alike — for birthdays, after exams, at company gatherings, or simply because friends are free.

Rooms usually cost less in the daytime and on weekday mornings than in the evening and at weekends, which is why a morning KTV session can make sense. Large KTV chains also serve meals, snacks and drinks, sometimes as a buffet, so a visit easily turns into a long party. Some families even keep a karaoke machine at home.

paras.text: Pinyin spelling: the final “-un”
After an initial consonant, u + en is written -un, although a short “e” sound can still be heard: 順 shùn (as in 六六大順), 春 chūn, 困 kùn.
After j, q and x, the same spelling “-un” stands for ü + n (the two dots are left off): 君 jūn, 群 qún, 訊 xùn.
Many Chinese punctuation marks work like English ones, but some are different. In Taiwan, marks such as 。，、 are printed in the middle of the character space rather than at the bottom.

separates items in a list: 茶、咖啡、甜點
quotation marks (Taiwan uses these corner brackets)

items: I can ask what time it is and tell the time.
I can say when and where something happens, and from when to when.
I can make a plan and fix a time to meet a friend.
I can talk about things I do every day or every week.
